title: Iter-3 R1-001 critical (ASK bit 127 mask) — FIXED in iter-4
description: Iter-4 verification of the iter-3 critical. traverseBigVector now strips bit 127 before extracting the upper 64 bits: `Number((BigInt(orderIdStr) & ASK_FLAG_MASK) >> 64n)` with `ASK_FLAG_MASK = (1n << 127n) - 1n`. Manual re-derivation against the captured chain-shape.md samples: bid `12377783720203182843884075n & ((1n<<127n)-1n) >> 64n = 671000n` (mask is a no-op since the value is ~83 bits; matches captured price 671000); ask `170141183460486719245069180370816077150n & ((1n<<127n)-1n) >> 64n = 948000n` (mask strips the ask flag bit; matches captured price 948000). Both match the canonical regression fixtures in chain-shape.md lines 129 and 218. Test fixtures in marketStats.test.ts use `makeBidOrderId` with the inverted-price convention, but those Order objects never pass through `traverseBigVector` — only real RPC-returned slices do — so the inverted-bid fixture path stays correctly on `decodeBidPrice` and the production path stays on the new bit-127-aware injection. No outstanding regression.
impact: iter-3 critical resolved. AC1.4 mid/spread/depth values are now computed against real chain prices on both sides of the book.
recommendation: Filing as info to record verification. No further action needed for this finding.

title: Iter-3 C027 disputed (closure-over-let in main.tsx) — FIXED in iter-4
description: Iter-4 verification of the C027 disputed cluster. `main.tsx` now uses a `buildDeps()` factory that captures `let packageId: string | undefined` in a single closure shared by both `loadManifest` and `fetchPoolStats`. No module-level mutable state, no `deps.loadManifest = …` reassignment. As a side bonus, `fetchPoolStats` now THROWS with an actionable wiring-bug message when called before manifest resolves, rather than silently issuing an `suix_queryEvents` filtered to `''` (the iter-3 silent-zero path).
impact: Closes the closure-over-let smell and tightens the cold-start contract. The sandbox-restart-mid-session staleness case (iter-3 R1-008) is still present — see R1-006 below — but the cold-start half is now loud.
recommendation: Filing as info. No further action for this specific defect.

title: rpc() still does not check response.ok; non-2xx surfaces JSON-parse SyntaxError verbatim (iter-2 R1-002 / iter-3 R1-002 unaddressed)
description: Carry-forward from iter-2 R1-002 / iter-3 R1-002. dataLayer.ts:45 `rpc()` calls `await fetch(...)` then immediately `await response.json()` without checking `response.ok`. On a 502/503 from the RPC port (e.g. during the well-documented 'sandbox restart with new packageId' scenario), the response body is HTML/text and `response.json()` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0`. That message reaches App.tsx's per-pool error banner verbatim — it points the operator at JSON parsing, not at the underlying HTTP failure or sandbox state. Iter-4 made no change here. (R1-008 from iter-3 also lives in this neighborhood: when the sandbox restarts mid-session, the cached `packageId` in main.tsx's `buildDeps()` closure is never refreshed; suix_queryEvents filtered on a stale packageId returns zero events with no signal — silent freshness failure for AC1.5. Filing the rpc() case here at high; the sandbox-restart-staleness case is filed separately at R1-006 to keep the rpc() cluster cohesive.)
impact: Operator-facing error text quality during sandbox restart and any non-2xx response. Mid-cycle sandbox restarts (a routine flow per chain-shape.md friction notes) produce confusing errors that misdirect debugging away from the actual failure mode. Combined with R1-005, this is the primary remaining 'silent or misleading degradation' surface in the data layer.
recommendation: Add `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(\`${method} HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text().catch(() => '<unreadable body>')}\`);` between fetch and json() in rpc(). The thrown error will propagate through `runDataLayer`'s allSettled and reach App.tsx's poolErrors banner with an actionable message. Same one-line fix recommended in iter-2 and iter-3 — still applies.

title: fetchPoolStats degrades to empty book when innerFields is null without surfacing the error (iter-3 R1-002 portion still present)
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R1-002, second half. resolvePoolInnerFields can `return null` (lines 114, 144) or `return fields` in a partial/degraded state (lines 121, 125, 134) without throwing. fetchPoolStats then constructs a default-empty PoolInnerState (line 384) when innerFields is null, and computeMarketStats yields all-undefined card stats — visually indistinguishable from 'pool is genuinely idle'. AC1.4's `bestBid <= mid <= bestAsk` invariant trivially holds when both sides are undefined, so the test gate cannot catch this. The iter-4 sweep did not touch resolvePoolInnerFields. The same silent-failure pattern as the iter-1 CR-1 cluster, partially carried forward.
impact: Operators cannot distinguish 'idle market' from 'shape parse failure' from 'sandbox restart with new package shape' from 'dynamic-field returned empty data'. AC1.4 / AC1.3 quietly pass with all-em-dash cards. This compounds with R1-003 — when the underlying RPC returns 4xx/5xx, the silent-degradation path here masks the failure shape further.
recommendation: In resolvePoolInnerFields, throw an actionable error at each early-return-null/degraded-fields branch naming WHICH expected field was absent (e.g. `Pool ${poolId}: content.fields.inner.fields.id.id absent — sandbox restart or shape drift suspected`). In fetchPoolStats, do not synthesise an empty PoolInnerState on null — let the rejection propagate to App.tsx's allSettled banner. App.tsx already handles propagated errors via the poolErrors UI (line 117-119).

title: fillFetcher pagination still unbounded across busy/sparse pool boundary (iter-3 R1-005 unaddressed)
description: Carry-forward from iter-2 R1-007 / iter-3 R1-005. The pagination loop has three stop conditions: `collected.length >= MAX_FILLS`, `crossedWindow`, or `!response.hasNextPage`. Both MAX_FILLS and crossedWindow only trigger after seeing OUR pool's events — `if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;` filters out cross-pool events BEFORE the window check. On a sandbox where our target pool is sparse and competing pools (DEEP/SUI vs SUI/USDC) are busy, every 50-event page may contain zero events for our pool, neither MAX_FILLS nor crossedWindow trip, and we paginate until hasNextPage:false — which on a continuously-active sandbox is effectively never (or until the 20s polling interval re-fires while the previous tick is still in flight, see R1-007). Iter-4 made no change here; the 'unused poolId param removed from buildQueryEventsFn' iter-4 cleanup did not touch this loop.
impact: Under multi-pool contention a single fetchFills invocation can issue hundreds of RPC calls and exceed the 20s refresh interval, compounding with R1-007 (no tick-id/abort guard — a slow tick can overwrite a fresh tick with stale data). AC1.5 sparkline freshness violated under realistic sandbox traffic patterns.
recommendation: Either (a) add a hard MAX_PAGES cap (e.g. 20) and surface a warning when reached, or (b) restructure to hoist the window check outside the per-pool filter — `if (nowMs - ev.timestampMs > DAY_MS) { crossedWindow = true; }` BEFORE the `if (ev.poolId !== poolId) continue;` check, so a chronologically-old event from any pool stops the descending walk. Option (b) is structurally cleaner since suix_queryEvents returns descending-by-time and old events from any pool legitimately mean we've reached the 24h horizon for ALL pools.

title: Polling refresh does not reload manifest; cached packageId stale across mid-session sandbox restart (iter-3 R1-008 partially fixed; mid-session case remains)
description: Carry-forward from iter-2 R1-005 / iter-3 R1-008. Iter-4 fixed the COLD-START half of this finding (fetchPoolStats now throws if called before loadManifest resolves), but the MID-SESSION half is unchanged: `packageId` is captured in the buildDeps closure on the first loadManifest call and never refreshed. App.tsx's polling useEffect (line 91-125) calls `deps.fetchPoolStats(p)` on every 20s tick but never re-invokes deps.loadManifest. If the sandbox is restarted mid-session and emits a new DeepBook packageId, the SPA keeps querying the stale id; suix_queryEvents filtered to a non-existent module returns empty pages, fetchFills converges to []) (subject to R1-005's pagination concern), and per-pool cards continue rendering with frozen sparklines. No UI signal of the underlying drift.
impact: AC1.5 freshness fails silently after a sandbox restart with no observable error. Operators see static sparklines and no banner. Compounds with R1-003 (the restart itself triggers transient 502s that surface as confusing JSON-parse errors before settling into silent-zero).
recommendation: Either (a) reload the manifest on every Nth polling tick (e.g. every 5th, ~100s) and update the captured packageId in the closure (would require restructuring buildDeps to expose a refresh hook), or (b) reload the manifest unconditionally on every tick (cheap; localnet.json is a tiny file served from disk via Vite middleware), or (c) at minimum, log a `console.warn` once per session if a tick produces zero events for ALL pools — that's the canary signal for 'sandbox restarted under us'. Option (b) is simplest and consistent with the spec's 'Slot 1 is read-only and dev-mode' framing.

title: App polling effect lacks tick-id/abort guard; stale tick can overwrite fresh state (iter-3 R1-004 unaddressed)
description: Carry-forward from iter-2 R1-008 / iter-3 R1-004 unchanged in iter-4. The polling useEffect runs `setInterval(20s)` and `Promise.allSettled` over all pools per tick. There is no guard against the previous tick still being in-flight: if a per-pool fetchPoolStats takes >20s (entirely possible during BigVector slice churn per chain-shape.md friction note, and made significantly worse by R1-005's unbounded pagination), tick N+1 starts before tick N's setState commits. Both ticks resolve in arbitrary order; setState applies last-writer-wins, which may be the older request's payload. There is also no AbortController for unmount cleanup; setState may fire on an unmounted component. The 'cancelled' flag in the initial-load effect (line 42, 86) is a good pattern but is not replicated in the refresh effect.
impact: Sparkline freshness AC (AC1.5) intermittently violated under slow/concurrent ticks: a slow fetch can overwrite a more recent fast fetch with stale data. Possible React 'state update on unmounted component' warning if unmount happens during a tick.
recommendation: Track a per-tick monotonic counter at tick start; only commit setState if the resolved tick is the latest counter value. Alternatively, use an AbortController per tick, abort on next tick start and on unmount, and wire it into the deps via fetch options (would also let R1-003's HTTP error surface promptly when the sandbox is being torn down). Minimum viable fix: replicate the `let cancelled = false` pattern from the initial-load effect — declare per-interval, set on cleanup, check before setState.

title: chain-shape.md decoding note still internally contradictory; types.ts comment perpetuates the wrong half (iter-3 R1-007 unaddressed)
description: Carry-forward from iter-3 R1-007. chain-shape.md still states two contradictory things about the bid encoding: (1) 'for bids it's [the encoding is] decreasing (inverted price), so a sort by raw order_id ascending lists ... bids worst-first' AND (2) 'price is the upper 64 bits; the lower 64 bits are an order-counter disambiguator'. Empirically, the captured bid order_id 12377783720203182843884075 has high-64 = 671000 = real price (plain), and low-64 = U64_MAX - some-counter (inverted counter, so descending sort puts newest bid first within a price level). So statement (2) is correct for the price half, statement (1) is a misread — the inversion is on the COUNTER, not on the price. The marketStats.test.ts fixture builder makeBidOrderId encodes `((U64_MAX - price) << 64) | counter`, which contradicts the captured chain shape but is internally consistent with `decodeBidPrice` in marketStats.ts. types.ts line 8 comment 'bid prices are stored inverted as U64_MAX - price' echoes the misread. This documentation drift is the upstream root cause of both the iter-2 CR-2 and iter-3 R1-001 critical bugs; iter-4 fixed the implementation correctly but did not update the prose.
impact: Future authors will get this wrong again. The next person to add a feature touching order_id decoding (e.g. for cancel-event handling, or a fee-tier lookup that uses price) will read the chain-shape.md note, conclude that bids are price-inverted, and either (a) introduce a new bug or (b) waste hours rediscovering the truth. Test fixtures perpetuate the false convention.
recommendation: Rewrite chain-shape.md lines 136-145 to: 'order_id u128 layout: bit 127 = ask flag (1=ask, 0=bid); bits 64-126 = price (plain integer, NOT inverted, on both sides); bits 0-63 = order counter (asks use ascending counter; bids use U64_MAX - counter so newest bid sorts first under ascending raw-id sort within a price level). To extract price: (id & ((1<<127)-1)) >> 64. The captured samples (ASK order_id 170141183460486719245069180370816077150 → price 948000; BID order_id 12377783720203182843884075 → price 671000) are the canonical regression fixtures.' Update types.ts line 8 comment to match. Optionally fix marketStats.test.ts makeBidOrderId to NOT invert price — but that change risks regression on the existing test math, so it can be deferred to a follow-up cycle as long as the prose is corrected.
evidence:
**Critical decoding note (sui-sdk + deepbook):** `order_id` is a u128 returned
by RPC as a decimal string. The high bits encode the limit price. For asks the
encoding is monotonically increasing in price; for bids it's decreasing
(inverted price), so a sort by raw `order_id` ascending lists asks
best-first / bids worst-first.

title: BigVector dynamic-field traversal cap of 64 silently truncates books with >64 slices
description: traverseBigVector calls suix_getDynamicFields with page-size=64 and `null` cursor, and never paginates further: `await rpc<DynamicFieldsResponse>(rpcUrl, 'suix_getDynamicFields', [bigVectorId, null, 64])` — then iterates `sliceList.data` once. The captured chain-shape.md shows BigVector with `max_slice_size: 64` and observed `length: 30`, so on the captured sandbox the single page is sufficient. But once a real pool exceeds 64 slices (achievable when the market maker fills more price levels, or when length grows past 64*64=4096 orders), this code silently truncates and computeMarketStats sees a partial book. The depth-at-±1% computation then produces a low-biased value with no error signal. AC1.4 mid still satisfies the bestBid<=mid<=bestAsk invariant against the truncated set. No test exercises >64 slices.
impact: Silent low-biased depth values once any pool's BigVector grows past 64 slice-leaves. The dashboard would render plausible-looking numbers that under-report depth by potentially 10x or more. Same silent-failure shape as the iter-1 CR-1 cluster.
recommendation: Replace the single-page call with a pagination loop using sliceList.nextCursor / hasNextPage, mirroring the pattern in fillFetcher.ts. Add a hard MAX_SLICES cap (e.g. 256, well above any realistic sandbox book) and surface a warning if hit. Alternatively, document the assumption explicitly in a code comment and add a test that asserts 64 is enough for the sandbox (will fail loudly if/when the assumption breaks).

title: computeMarketStats one-sided fallback labels stats `bestAsk * 0.99..1.01` as `depthWithinOnePercent` of a non-existent mid
description: When only one side of the book is populated (the other returned [] from traverseBigVector — exactly the case during BigVector slice churn or after R1-009 truncation of one side), computeMarketStats falls back to anchoring depth to bestBid*0.99..1.01 OR bestAsk*0.99..1.01 (independently). midPrice and spread remain undefined (which is fine — PoolCard renders '—'), but `depthWithinOnePercent` is reported as a non-zero number. The PoolCard label is 'depth within ±1% of mid'. With no mid, the displayed depth value is 'depth within ±1% of best-{bid|ask}', not 'depth within ±1% of mid'. The label and the value diverge. AC1.3 requires the six labeled fields; this is a label/value inconsistency, not a missing field. Found while reviewing the iter-4-untouched marketStats.ts during the polling/freshness audit triggered by R1-007.
impact: Operators reading a one-sided pool see a depth value that semantically diverges from its label. Low because (a) one-sided books are transient, (b) the magnitude difference is small (1% off either bound vs ±1% off mid is ~0.5% asymmetry), and (c) no test captures the issue. But the inconsistency is the kind of thing that erodes trust in the dashboard.
recommendation: Either (a) report `depthWithinOnePercent: undefined` when midPrice is undefined and let the PoolCard render '—' (most defensible, mirrors mid/spread behavior), or (b) keep the fallback compute but rename the field to `depthWithinOnePercentOfReference` and have the card label adapt. Option (a) is simplest.
